entries.label: Airborne Networks

entries.quote: An Internet in the sky could let planes fly safely without ground controllers.

entries.label: Quantum Wires
key_players: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
entries.quote: Wires spun from carbon nanotubes could carry electricity farther and more efficiently.

entries.label: Silicon Photonics
entries.quote: Making the material of computer chips emit light could speed data flow.

entries.label: Metabolomics
entries.quote: A new diagnostic tool could mean spotting diseases earlier and more easily.

entries.label: Magnetic-Resonance Force Microscopy
entries.quote: The promise is a 3-D view of the molecular world.

entries.quote: Nanotubes make possible ultradense data storage.

entries.label: Bacterial Factories
entries.quote: Overhauling a microbe's metabolism could yield a cheap malaria drug.

entries.label: Enviromatics
key_players: Pennsylvania State University Center for Environmental Informatics
entries.quote: Computer forecasts enhance farm production and species diversity.

entries.label: Cell-Phone Viruses

entries.quote: Mating robotics with the nervous system creates a new generation of artificial limbs that work like the real thing.

notes: Ten entries. Published in the May 2005 issue, not January/February. No availability field. Forward timings from body text are in entry notes; they are often a quoted person's prediction. Read through a summarising fetch; medium confidence.
